blocks.body: After storms like 2013, many Elmhurst homeowners want a generator that starts on its own when the power goes out, keeping the sump pump, furnace and refrigerator running. A natural gas generator needs a line sized for its load plus everything already in the house. We size and run the line and pressure-test it. A licensed electrician installs the transfer switch.

blocks.h2: How We Plan the Route for a New Gas Line
blocks.body: We start at the meter and follow the existing pipe to find the best place to branch off. Then we plan a route through the basement or crawl space that's easy to support and service. For outdoor lines, we decide between running along the house or underground. A shorter, simpler route usually means a lower price and a faster install.

blocks.h2: Gas Line Installation Questions From Elmhurst Homeowners

items.q: Can you run a gas line for a generator?
items.answer: Yes, sized for the generator plus everything else on the system.

items.q: Can I switch my range from electric to gas?
items.answer: Usually. We run a branch line and install a shutoff behind the range.
Yes, where the city requires one.

items.q: Can my existing pipe handle a new appliance?
items.answer: We calculate the load and check the pipe size before connecting.

items.q: How long does a generator gas line take?
items.answer: Often a day, depending on the distance from the meter.

items.q: Can you run gas to a detached garage?
items.answer: Yes, with an underground line sized for the heater or appliance and a shutoff at the garage.

items.q: How much does gas line installation cost in Elmhurst?
items.preview: It depends on the run. You'll approve a flat price first.
items.answer: It depends on the length of the run, the appliance and the route. You'll approve a flat-rate price before we start.
